data.title: About Ani
data.intro: European master hairstylist, former director-level stylist at José Eber and Vidal Sassoon, now taking clients in South Orange County.

content.headline: Hair is personal. So is the way I work.

children.text: For the professional who wants to refine or refresh a look, I offer something that is hard to find: time, technique, and honesty about what will suit you.

I trained in Europe and spent more than ten years as a director-level stylist at José Eber and Vidal Sassoon. I have styled hair for fashion shows and for Fendi, W magazine, and Roxy, and I have been featured in Orange Coast and Women magazine.

Today I see clients one at a time at James Mathew Salon. Many have been with me for more than fifteen years. Some fly in from Canada, Peru, and Israel. They come back because their hair looks like them, only better, and because it is easy to care for at home.
Outside the salon I love exercise, gardening, and anything that keeps us healthy. Ask me about the bananas and coffee I grow in my backyard.

$media.alt: Warm afternoon light across a minimal styling station with round mirrors and a pale wood counter

data.title: Booking and cancellation policy
data.intro: How booking, changes, and cancellations work.

children.text: Booking
You can book online at any time. Your appointment is confirmed as soon as you see the confirmation screen, and a confirmation email follows. Nothing is charged online; you pay at the salon.
Changes and cancellations
Please cancel at least 24 hours before your appointment, using the link in your confirmation email or by calling. Late cancellations and missed appointments keep another client from that time.
Running late
If you are running more than 15 minutes late, please call. I will do everything I can, but I may need to shorten the service or move it so the next client is not kept waiting.

data.title: Privacy
data.intro: What this website collects and how it is used.

children.text: What we collect
When you book or send a message, we collect your name, email, phone number, and anything you choose to write. We use it only to schedule your appointment, remind you of it, and reply to you.
Analytics
This site counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies and does not track you across other websites.
Product links
Some product links are affiliate links. If you buy through one, the store may pay a small commission. The price you pay does not change.
Your choices
To see, change, or delete the details we hold about you, call or email and we will take care of it.

data.title: Women's precision cut
data.summary: A consultation, shampoo, a precision cut shaped for your texture, and a finish you can recreate at home.

$media.alt: A stylist cuts a section of long, wet dark hair with scissors and a comb

children.text: A precision cut is the foundation of everything else. I study how your hair grows, where it wants to fall, and how much time you really spend on it in the morning. Then I cut for that, so it looks finished on the days you air dry it too.

Curly, straight, fine, thick, or difficult: every texture needs its own technique. Curls are shaped where they live, fine hair gets weight kept where it matters, and thick hair is lightened from the inside so it moves.
What to expect
A conversation about your routine, your photos, and what has not worked before.
Shampoo and a scalp massage.
The cut, then a blow-dry or diffuse with a short lesson on how to style it yourself.
Come with your hair the way you usually wear it, so I can see your everyday style.

data.title: Men's cut
data.summary: A tailored scissor cut with a shampoo and finish. Clean lines that still look right three weeks later.

$media.alt: A scissor and comb cut on a man's salt-and-pepper hair, seen from behind

children.text: A men's cut should look sharp on day one and grow out without losing its shape. I work mostly with scissors over comb, so the shape follows your head and your hairline instead of a clipper guard.
What to expect
A quick consultation about length, part, and how you style it.
Shampoo, cut, and a clean finish at the neck and around the ears.
A product recommendation if you want one, and how much to use.

data.title: Fringe trim
data.summary: A quick trim to keep bangs and face-framing pieces in shape between cuts.

data.title: Gray blending
data.summary: Soft, multi-tonal color that blends gray instead of covering it, so regrowth is gentle and visits are further apart.

$media.alt: A client's chin-length silver bob with soft movement, cut by Ani

children.text: Gray blending is for clients who are tired of a hard line at the root every three weeks. Instead of one solid color, I weave in lowlights and highlights close to your natural shades. The gray becomes part of the color rather than something to hide.
Some clients use it to stretch time between appointments. Others use it as a gentle path to going fully silver. Either way, it should look like your own hair, only brighter.
What to expect
A color consultation in natural light to choose tones that suit your skin.
Hand-placed lowlights and highlights, then a gloss to tie them together.
A blow-dry and a plan for your next visit, usually in 8 to 12 weeks.
Prices start here and depend on length and density. I confirm the price before we begin.

data.title: Root touch-up
data.summary: All-over color refreshed at the root, with a gloss on the lengths for shine.

$media.alt: A colorist paints lightener onto a section of long dark hair over a board, with foils below

data.title: Highlights and dimensional color
data.summary: Hand-placed highlights or balayage for depth and brightness that grows out softly.

$media.alt: Long brunette waves with soft caramel dimension, colored and styled by Ani

children.text: Dimensional color adds light where the sun would naturally hit and depth underneath, so your hair looks thicker and more alive. I choose foils, balayage, or both, depending on how bright you want to go and how often you want to come in.
What to expect
A consultation about your color history, so the result is predictable.
Lightening and toning, then a gloss for shine.
A blow-dry and the home care that keeps the tone true.
Big changes, like blonde to brunette, may take two visits. Book a color consultation first if you are unsure.

data.title: Blowout
data.summary: A shampoo and smooth, bouncy blow-dry that lasts for days.

$media.alt: A glossy, bouncy blowout in long highlighted hair, seen from behind in a bright salon

children.text: Clients with curly, thick, or frizzy hair often book a weekly blowout with me. It is the fastest way to look polished for the week, and the right technique keeps the shape for days without damage.

data.title: Special occasion styling
data.summary: Styling for weddings, galas, and photos: soft waves, an elegant updo, or a sleek finish.

$media.alt: Warm afternoon light across a minimal styling station with round mirrors and a pale wood counter

children.text: I have styled hair for fashion shows and magazine shoots, and I bring the same care to your event. Send me a photo of your outfit when you book, and come with clean, dry hair unless we plan a shampoo.

data.title: Brazilian Blowout smoothing
data.summary: A professional smoothing treatment that removes frizz and adds shine for up to 12 weeks, with no downtime.

$media.alt: Sleek, frizz-free brown hair over the shoulders of a white shirt, seen from behind

children.text: The Brazilian Blowout creates a protective layer around each hair to smooth the cuticle and eliminate frizz. Hair stays soft and moves naturally. It does not look flat or chemically straight.
There is no downtime: you can wash, air dry, and wear your hair up the same day. Results last up to 12 weeks with the right shampoo.
What to expect
A strand check and a shampoo to prepare the hair.
The smoothing solution is applied, dried, and sealed with a flat iron.
Aftercare advice and a sulfate-free routine to make it last.
The price depends on length and thickness. I confirm it before we begin.

data.title: Kérastase ritual
data.summary: A personalized Kérastase treatment for dry, damaged, or color-treated hair, with a scalp massage.

$media.alt: A client's long hair being rinsed at a white salon basin during a treatment

children.text: Every head of hair needs something different. After a quick diagnosis of your hair and scalp, I choose the Kérastase treatment that fits: deep nourishment for dry ends, strength for color-damaged hair, or balance for an oily scalp.
It is a lovely add-on to a cut or color, or a quiet half hour on its own.

data.title: Hair extensions consultation
data.summary: We talk through length, volume, and the right method for your hair, and match color.

$media.alt: A stylist fits extension wefts into long platinum hair in front of a gilded mirror

children.text: Extensions can add length, fill in thin areas, or simply give more volume. The method matters: it has to suit your own hair and your routine, and it has to be invisible. I match color in person and give you a firm quote for the full service.

data.title: Color consultation
data.summary: Planning a big change, or correcting color from elsewhere? Let's look at it together first.

data.title: Thinning hair consultation
data.summary: A private conversation about shedding or thinning, and a plan: the cut, color, and care that help.

$media.alt: A hand draws a wooden comb through long, straight auburn hair

children.text: Thinning hair is common, and it is not something you have to live with quietly. In a private consultation we look at your scalp and hair together, talk about what changed and when, and build a plan.

Often that means a cut that puts weight where it helps, color that adds the look of density, and a scalp routine. If anything suggests a medical cause, I will tell you, and suggest you see your doctor or a dermatologist.

data.title: Genesis Anti Hair-Fall Fortifying Serum
data.note: A light leave-in serum for the scalp. I suggest it to clients who notice more hair in the brush: used every day, it strengthens the hair from the root and reduces breakage.

data.title: Genesis Bain Hydra-Fortifiant Shampoo
data.note: A gentle shampoo for hair that breaks and sheds easily. It cleans the scalp without stripping, which matters more than most people think.

data.title: Wide-Tooth Detangling Comb
data.note: The single cheapest thing that saves hair. Comb wet hair from the ends up, never from the root down, and you will lose far less to breakage.

data.title: Mulberry Silk Pillowcase
data.note: Cotton grabs the hair all night. Silk lets it glide, so you wake up with less frizz, fewer tangles, and a blowout that lasts a day longer.

data.title: Elixir Ultime L'Huile Originale
data.note: My favorite finishing oil. Two drops on the ends after blow-drying for shine and softness, without making fine hair heavy.

data.title: Blond Absolu Bain Ultra-Violet
data.note: A purple shampoo that keeps silver and blonde bright instead of yellow. Use it once or twice a week, not every wash.

data.title: Açaí Anti-Frizz Shampoo
data.note: Made to protect a Brazilian Blowout. Sulfate-free and gentle, so the smoothing lasts the full 12 weeks.

data.title: Résistance Ciment Thermique
data.note: A heat protectant that also repairs. Use it before every blow-dry if your hair is colored or fragile.

data.title: Microfiber Hair Towel
data.note: Rubbing hair with a cotton towel roughs up the cuticle. Blot with microfiber instead, especially curls, and you will see less frizz.

data.title: What is the best way to care for curly hair?
data.summary: Get a cut shaped for your curls, keep them hydrated, blot instead of rubbing, and never brush them dry. Let curls dry undisturbed, or use a diffuser on low.

children.text: Curls need moisture, a cut that respects how they fall, and as little friction as possible.
Start with the right cut
Curls shrink and spring differently on every head. I shape them where they live, so the cut looks balanced when your hair dries naturally, not only after a blowout.
Everyday routine
Detangle only when wet and full of conditioner, with your fingers or a wide-tooth comb.
Blot with a microfiber towel or a cotton T-shirt; never rub.
Apply a leave-in while the hair is soaking wet to lock in moisture.
Diffuse on low heat, or let curls dry without touching them.

$media.alt: Long, defined spiral curls seen from behind against a cream wall

data.title: Why does my hair color fade so fast?
data.summary: Hot water, harsh shampoos, sun, and heat styling wash color out. Wash less often in cool water, use a color-safe shampoo, and protect your hair from heat.

children.text: Color molecules escape every time the cuticle opens. Most fading comes from a few everyday habits:
Hot showers.
Rinse in lukewarm or cool water.
Washing every day.
Two or three times a week is plenty for most hair.
Harsh shampoo.
Choose a gentle, color-safe formula.
Sun and heat.
Use a heat protectant before styling and a hat at the beach.
Red and copper tones fade fastest. A gloss between color appointments brings the shine and tone back in half an hour.

$media.alt: Long brunette waves with soft caramel dimension, colored and styled by Ani

data.title: How do I make my Brazilian Blowout last?
data.summary: Wash with a sulfate-free shampoo, keep chlorine and salt water off your hair, and blow-dry with low heat. With the right care, results last up to 12 weeks.

children.text: The Brazilian Blowout works from the first wash, and the way you care for it decides whether it lasts six weeks or twelve.
Use a sulfate-free shampoo and conditioner. Sulfates strip the protective layer.
Rinse with fresh water after the pool or the ocean, or wear a cap.
Blow-dry with a round brush on medium heat when you want it extra sleek. Air drying is fine too.
Book your next treatment when the frizz starts to come back, usually after 10 to 12 weeks.

$media.alt: Sleek, frizz-free brown hair over the shoulders of a white shirt, seen from behind

data.title: How often should I get a haircut?
data.summary: Short hair every 4 to 6 weeks, medium length every 6 to 8, and long hair every 8 to 12. Come sooner if the ends feel dry or the shape stops falling into place.

children.text: It depends on the length and on the shape you want to keep.
Short cuts and men's cuts:
every 4 to 6 weeks. A few millimeters change everything.
Bobs and medium length:
every 6 to 8 weeks to keep the line crisp.
Long hair:
every 8 to 12 weeks to keep the ends healthy while you grow it.
A good precision cut grows out gracefully, so you should not feel you are fighting your hair in week five. If you are, the cut is not working for your texture, and we should change it.

$media.alt: A stylist cuts a section of long, wet dark hair with scissors and a comb

data.title: How do I blend gray instead of covering it?
data.summary: Switch from solid coverage to gray blending: soft lowlights and highlights that let your silver become part of the color, so regrowth is gentle and visits stretch to 8 to 12 weeks.

children.text: Solid color creates a hard line the moment the gray grows in. Gray blending works with your natural silver instead of against it.
How it works

I place fine lowlights and highlights in shades close to your own, then finish with a gloss. The gray becomes another tone in the mix. When it grows out, there is no stripe at the part, just a softer version of the same color.
Going fully silver

If you want to stop coloring altogether, blending is the gentlest way through it. A shorter cut speeds things up. One of my clients went from a long bob to a short, textured cut with soft fringe, and the silver finally looked intentional instead of like waiting for roots.
Keep silver bright
Use a purple shampoo once or twice a week to keep yellow tones away.
Protect from heat and sun, which turn gray brassy.
Finish with a little oil: silver hair is often drier and loves shine.

$media.alt: A client's chin-length silver bob with soft movement, cut by Ani

data.title: What can I do to stop my hair from falling out?
data.summary: First, find out why: see your doctor for a blood test if the shedding is new. Then be gentle with your hair, care for your scalp every day, and get a cut that makes the most of the hair you have.

children.text: This is the question I hear most, and I understand how worrying it is. The good news: in most cases there is a lot we can do, and the routine below is the one I give my own clients.
1. Find out why it is happening

Everyone loses about 50 to 100 hairs a day. If you are suddenly losing much more, something usually changed about three months earlier: stress, illness, surgery, a new medication, a baby, or a crash diet.

If the shedding is new or heavy, ask your doctor for a blood test. Low iron, thyroid changes, and low vitamin D are common and very treatable causes. Patchy loss or an itchy, sore scalp is a reason to see a dermatologist.
2. Be gentle with the hair you have
Detangle wet hair with a wide-tooth comb, starting at the ends.
Skip tight ponytails and buns; use a soft scrunchie or a claw clip.
Turn the heat down on your dryer and irons, and always use a heat protectant.
Sleep on silk so the hair is not rubbed and pulled all night.
3. Care for your scalp every day

Healthy hair grows from a healthy scalp. Wash with a gentle shampoo, massage the scalp for a minute or two while you do, and use a fortifying scalp serum daily. Give it three months: hair grows slowly, and so does the improvement.
4. Let the cut and color work for you

Long, heavy hair pulls and shows the scalp. A shorter shape with soft layers puts the weight where it creates fullness. Color helps too: a few lowlights close to your scalp color make the part look less sparse.
If you are worried, book a thinning hair consultation. We will look at it together, privately, and make a plan.

$media.alt: A hand draws a wooden comb through long, straight auburn hair
